description: REQ-P4's edge case states "UserPromptSubmit の他 entry（cozempic 由来含む）は一切変更してはならない", but PROP-P4's acceptance criteria only assert (a) zero ssot-guard command entries remain under UserPromptSubmit and (b) exactly one remains under SessionStart and (c) the file is valid JSON. On-disk verification of the live `~/.claude/settings.json` shows the ssot-guard command is NOT its own top-level array entry -- it is packed together with `disk-guard.sh` inside the SAME matcher-group object: `hooks.UserPromptSubmit == [{"matcher":"*","hooks":[{command: ssot-guard.sh},{command: disk-guard.sh}]}, {"matcher":"","hooks":[{command: <cozempic inline script>}]}]`. Because ssot-guard.sh and disk-guard.sh share one matcher-group's `hooks` array, a plausible-but-wrong implementation (e.g. deleting the whole first matcher-group object instead of surgically removing just the ssot-guard command from its `hooks` array) would still make PROP-P4's three listed assertions pass (0 ssot-guard hits, SessionStart still has 1, JSON still valid) while silently deleting disk-guard.sh -- a hook the project's own CLAUDE.md disk-hygiene rules treat as important. No PROP-P4 assertion checks that disk-guard.sh survives.
suggestedFix: Add an explicit PROP-P4 shell assertion confirming the disk-guard command entry is unchanged/still present under UserPromptSubmit after the edit, e.g. `jq -e '[.hooks.UserPromptSubmit // [] | .[].hooks[]?.command | select(test("disk-guard"))] | length == 1' ~/.claude/settings.json`, and/or require a byte-identical diff of the surviving (non-ssot-guard) hook objects before/after, mirroring the approach already used for REQ-SAFE-3's invariants.
